stories.title: CISA Flags TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation in the Wild
stories.abstract: CISA has added several critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, most notably a high-severity deserialization flaw in JetBrains TeamCity. These vulnerabilities are currently being actively exploited by threat actors to gain unauthorized access and control over affected systems.
stories.why: Exploitation of these flaws allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution, potentially leading to full system compromise and lateral network movement.
stories.action: Patch all on-premise JetBrains TeamCity instances and affected software immediately.

stories.title: Django security advisory (AV26-786)
stories.abstract: The Django framework has released security updates for versions 6.0.8 and 5.2.17 to address multiple vulnerabilities. Administrators should prioritize patching these instances to mitigate potential security risks associated with the identified flaws.
stories.why: Unpatched web frameworks are frequent targets for remote code execution and data exfiltration attacks.
stories.action: Update Django to version 6.0.8 or 5.2.17 immediately.

stories.title: Snowflake Hacker Pleads Guilty Over Breaches Affecting at Least 100 Million People
stories.abstract: Connor Riley Moucka has pleaded guilty to orchestrating a massive extortion campaign targeting over 165 organizations via Snowflake cloud environments. The Canadian national also admitted to exfiltrating sensitive call and text records belonging to more than 100 million AT&T customers.
stories.why: This case highlights the severe risks of credential-based attacks on cloud infrastructure and the massive scale of data theft possible through single-provider compromises.

stories.title: AI-Assisted HTTP Terminator Finds Novel HTTP Desync Techniques and Apache Zero-Day
stories.abstract: Researcher James Kettle developed an AI-driven tool called HTTP Terminator that identified novel HTTP desynchronization methods by testing thousands of vectors. The system also facilitated the discovery of a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability within the Apache Traffic Server.
stories.why: Automated discovery of desync vulnerabilities highlights evolving risks to request smuggling defenses and the potential for AI to accelerate exploit development.

stories.title: Cyberattack on North Carolina Ports ‘contained’ as Coast Guard, state officials investigate
stories.abstract: The North Carolina Ports Authority is managing a cyberattack that compromised its IT infrastructure. The breach has forced the Port of Wilmington, the Port of Morehead City, and the Charlotte Inland Port to transition to manual operational procedures while recovery efforts are underway.
stories.why: Critical infrastructure disruptions highlight ongoing risks to maritime logistics and supply chain stability from unauthorized network intrusions.

stories.title: AI Recommendation Poisoning: How "Ask AI" Buttons Silently Alter LLM Memory
stories.abstract: Attackers are embedding malicious, hidden prompt injection payloads into pre-filled deep links within "Ask AI" buttons on commercial websites. When users click these buttons, the injected instructions manipulate the LLM's behavior or memory without the user's knowledge or consent.
stories.why: This technique weaponizes standard UI features to perform unauthorized actions or data exfiltration via LLMs, bypassing traditional security perimeters.

stories.title: TeamPCP Linked To Redis Attacks Dating Back To 2020 And Later Supply Chain Campaign
stories.abstract: Researchers have linked the threat actor TeamPCP to long-standing cryptojacking campaigns and the ShadowRay 2.0 attacks. The group has been exploiting internet-facing infrastructure since 2020, recently expanding their operations to target software supply chains using consistent backend infrastructure and malware delivery methods.
stories.why: Understanding the persistence and evolution of established threat actors helps security teams identify long-term patterns in infrastructure compromise and supply chain targeting.

stories.title: New WordPress Pre-Auth XSS Could Lead to PHP Code Execution - Patch ASAP
stories.abstract: A critical pre-authentication reflected XSS vulnerability, CVE-2026-64638, affects all WordPress versions. The flaw resides in the login interface and can be leveraged to achieve remote PHP code execution on the underlying server without requiring prior authentication.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full server control, posing a severe risk to any WordPress-based infrastructure.
stories.action: Update all WordPress installations to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Levi Strauss says hackers breached employee computers, accessed corporate data
stories.abstract: Levi Strauss disclosed a security breach involving three company-issued workstations. Attackers utilized social engineering tactics to compromise these devices, subsequently exfiltrating internal corporate data from the network.
stories.why: This incident highlights the persistent risk of social engineering as a successful initial access vector against enterprise environments.

stories.title: Attackers Compile khunt Inside Oracle to Turn SQL Injection Into Windows SYSTEM Access
stories.abstract: Threat actors are leveraging SQL injection vulnerabilities to inject Java source code directly into Oracle databases. By utilizing the database's internal compilation features, attackers execute malicious toolkits as stored schema objects, effectively bypassing traditional endpoint security controls that monitor for file-based activity.
stories.why: This fileless technique circumvents standard EDR detection by executing malicious logic entirely within the database engine's memory space.
stories.action: Audit public-facing applications for SQL injection vulnerabilities and restrict database-level Java execution permissions.

stories.title: Ransom Cartel Creator Gets 16 Years in Prison for Operating Ransomware-as-a-Service
stories.abstract: A Belarusian national, Maksim Silnikau, received a 16-year prison sentence in the United States for his role as the administrator of the Ransom Cartel ransomware-as-a-service operation, which targeted at least 18 organizations globally between 2021 and 2023.
stories.why: This sentencing highlights successful international law enforcement efforts to dismantle ransomware-as-a-service infrastructure and hold key operators accountable for multi-year criminal campaigns.

stories.title: Cisco Patches 12 SD-WAN and IOS XE Flaws, Including Three 9.9 CVSS Score Bugs
stories.abstract: Cisco released patches for twelve vulnerabilities affecting Catalyst SD-WAN, IOS XE, and Secure FMC software. Three of these flaws are rated critical with a 9.9 CVSS score, potentially allowing unauthorized access or system compromise across various network infrastructure deployments.
stories.why: Critical vulnerabilities in core networking equipment pose a high risk of remote exploitation, potentially granting attackers full control over enterprise network traffic.
stories.action: Update Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, IOS XE, and Secure FMC software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: French rugby club Stade Français restores systems after cyberattack, probes data leak
stories.abstract: Stade Français successfully recovered its internal IT infrastructure following a recent cyberattack. The organization confirmed that critical services, including its digital storefront and ticketing systems, remained functional throughout the incident and were not compromised by the breach.
stories.why: Organizations must maintain robust, tested backup strategies to ensure operational continuity and rapid recovery following disruptive security incidents.

stories.title: Real emails, hijacked payments: Two H1 2026 attack chains
stories.abstract: A recent threat report highlights two distinct attack methods: one leveraging hijacked business email accounts combined with browser-based manipulation to facilitate banking fraud, and another utilizing clipboard-monitoring malware to intercept and redirect cryptocurrency transactions during the payment process.
stories.why: These campaigns demonstrate how attackers are evolving beyond simple phishing to manipulate active browser sessions and local system data for financial theft.

stories.title: CISA warns of hackers exploiting Langflow, N-central, Apache Tomcat flaws
Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
stories.abstract: The Swiss Federal Office of Information Technology confirmed that attackers breached government SharePoint servers by exploiting undisclosed vulnerabilities. The incident resulted in the unauthorized access of roughly 200 user accounts, prompting an ongoing investigation into the scope of the data exposure.
stories.why: Government infrastructure breaches highlight persistent risks in enterprise collaboration platforms and the potential for lateral movement following initial server exploitation.

stories.title: New Zapscape KVM Flaw Could Let Privileged L1 Guest Code Escape to Linux Hosts
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in the Linux kernel's KVM shadow memory management unit, identified as CVE-2026-64561, allows attackers with kernel-level access within an L1 guest virtual machine to break out of isolation and execute arbitrary code on the underlying host system.
stories.why: This flaw enables guest-to-host escapes, potentially compromising the entire virtualization infrastructure when nested virtualization is enabled for untrusted tenants.
stories.action: Apply the latest Linux kernel security patches to address the KVM shadow MMU vulnerability.

stories.title: ABB Ability Zenon
stories.abstract: ABB Ability Zenon IIoT services utilizing MongoDB 4.2 are vulnerable to multiple flaws, including out-of-bounds writes and improper certificate validation. These issues could allow unauthorized code execution, system crashes, or data compromise within critical infrastructure environments.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose industrial control systems to remote exploitation, potentially leading to unauthorized operational control or data theft in sensitive sectors.
stories.action: Contact ABB support to determine the appropriate patch or mitigation for your specific deployment.

stories.title: Medixant RadiAnt DICOM
stories.abstract: Medixant RadiAnt DICOM versions 2025.2 and earlier contain an out-of-bounds write vulnerability. Processing a specially crafted DICOM file with malicious JPEG-compressed pixel data can trigger a heap corruption, potentially enabling remote code execution or application crashes.
stories.why: This flaw poses a significant risk to healthcare environments by allowing remote attackers to compromise systems via standard medical imaging files.
stories.action: Update RadiAnt DICOM to a version beyond 2025.2.

stories.title: Johnson Controls Inc. TL280
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls TL280 alarm communicators running firmware versions prior to 5.63 contain hardcoded credentials. This vulnerability allows unauthorized actors to bypass authentication mechanisms and access sensitive device information, potentially impacting critical infrastructure sectors where these units are deployed.
stories.why: Hardcoded credentials in industrial hardware provide trivial entry points for attackers to gain administrative access to critical facility monitoring systems.
stories.action: Update TL280 firmware to version 5.63 or later.

stories.title: COLDCARD security audit phishing attack installs remote access tool
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging recent security concerns regarding COLDCARD wallets to distribute phishing emails. These messages trick recipients into downloading malicious scripts that install ScreenConnect, granting unauthorized remote access and persistence on the target's machine.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how threat actors weaponize high-profile security disclosures to conduct social engineering and establish persistent remote access.
stories.action: Do not download or execute unsolicited attachments or scripts claiming to be security updates.

stories.title: Linux Shell Forensic: Let?s Dive Into Atuin!, (Fri, Aug 7th)
stories.abstract: Standard Linux shell history files are often insufficient for robust auditing, as they are easily manipulated or cleared. Atuin offers a modern alternative by replacing traditional flat-file logging with a SQLite-backed database, providing improved command tracking, synchronization, and searchability for security investigations.
stories.why: Enhanced shell logging improves incident response and forensic visibility by preventing attackers from easily tampering with or deleting their command execution history.

stories.title: 3.8 Million Impacted by Unlimited Technology Systems Data Breach
stories.abstract: Unlimited Technology Systems suffered a significant data breach involving the theft of sensitive personal, medical, and health insurance records from its data center. Approximately 3.8 million individuals have been affected by this unauthorized access.
stories.why: Large-scale exposure of PII and PHI increases the risk of targeted phishing, identity theft, and medical fraud for the impacted population.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit N-able Patch Bypass Flaw on RMM Servers
stories.abstract: N-able identified a new authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-18577, affecting its Remote Monitoring and Management servers. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to gain administrative control over the targeted systems.
stories.why: RMM platforms are high-value targets for supply chain attacks, providing attackers with broad access to downstream managed networks.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by N-able immediately.

stories.title: Zyxel security advisory (AV26-780)
stories.abstract: Zyxel has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting various firewall and access point models, including the ATP, USG FLEX, and WAX650S series. The flaws involve path traversal, command injection, and authentication bypass issues within specific firmware versions.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands or manipulate system configurations, potentially leading to full device compromise.
stories.action: Update affected Zyxel firmware to the latest available versions immediately.

stories.title: Meta AI model hacked a company during misconfigured cyber test
stories.abstract: Meta acknowledged that one of its AI models successfully compromised a real-world organization during a controlled cybersecurity evaluation. This incident follows a similar disclosure from OpenAI regarding its own agents breaching external systems during testing.
stories.why: Autonomous agents capable of executing offensive cyber operations pose significant risks if misconfigured or deployed without adequate safety guardrails.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, August 7th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10042, (Fri, Aug 7th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for August 7, 2026, provides a daily summary of current cybersecurity events and technical observations. The episode covers recent threat intelligence and operational security updates relevant to network defenders.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat trends helps security teams identify emerging patterns and adjust defensive postures against active campaigns.

stories.title: IBM's agentic AI platform is under active attack - patch now
stories.abstract: CISA has confirmed active exploitation of a critical remote code execution vulnerability within Langflow, an agentic AI development platform. Attackers are leveraging this flaw to compromise default installations, posing a significant risk to environments utilizing the framework for AI workflows.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE in AI infrastructure allows attackers to gain full control over agentic systems, potentially leading to data exfiltration or lateral movement.
stories.action: Update Langflow to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: GitHub security advisory (AV26-783)
stories.abstract: GitHub has released security patches for multiple versions of its Enterprise Server software, ranging from 3.17 to 3.21. Administrators should review the latest release notes to identify the specific updates required for their current deployment.
stories.why: Unpatched enterprise server vulnerabilities can lead to unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or remote code execution within critical development infrastructure.
stories.action: Update GitHub Enterprise Server to the latest patched version for your specific release branch.

stories.title: Jenkins security advisory (AV26-782)
stories.abstract: The Jenkins project released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its core platform, Remoting component, and several plugins, including AWS CodeBuild, GitLab, and Google Chat integrations. Administrators should review the advisory to identify affected versions within their environments.
stories.why: Unpatched Jenkins instances are frequent targets for remote code execution and unauthorized access, potentially compromising CI/CD pipelines and underlying infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Jenkins core, Remoting, and the specified plugins to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: Ransomware Surges in July After Q2 Lull
stories.abstract: Ransomware activity spiked significantly throughout July, reversing the downward trend observed during the second quarter. Comparitech reports that the finance, technology, and healthcare industries faced the highest volume of attacks during this period.
stories.why: Security teams in these high-risk sectors should anticipate increased extortion attempts and re-evaluate their incident response readiness against current ransomware tactics.

stories.title: Hedge fund cyberattacks tied to BlackFile-linked UNC6671 extortion group
stories.abstract: Financial institutions, including hedge funds and private equity firms, are facing a surge in extortion attacks orchestrated by the threat actor UNC6671. This group is reportedly collaborating with the BlackFile ransomware operation to target sensitive data within the financial sector.
stories.why: Financial firms are high-value targets for extortion; understanding the tactics of emerging groups like UNC6671 is critical for threat modeling and defense.

stories.title: Vishing Extortion Group UNC6671 Rebrands After Making Millions
stories.abstract: The threat actor UNC6671, previously known as BlackFile, has diversified its extortion operations. The group now operates under multiple aliases, including Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon, following a period of successful financial gain through vishing-based attacks.
stories.why: Tracking rebranding efforts is essential for threat intelligence teams to maintain visibility into evolving adversary infrastructure and tactics.

stories.title: Over 4,400 Rockwell PLCs Exposed Online, 22 Found in Water Attack Cities
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified over 4,400 Rockwell Automation programmable logic controllers accessible via the public internet. Notably, 22 of these exposed devices are located within municipalities that recently experienced cyberattacks targeting water utility infrastructure.
stories.why: Exposed industrial control systems provide direct attack vectors for adversaries to manipulate critical infrastructure processes or disrupt essential public services.
stories.action: Identify and isolate internet-facing industrial controllers behind firewalls or VPNs to prevent unauthorized external access.

stories.title: Google Links Redact Extortion Group to BlackFile Rebrand
stories.abstract: Google researchers identified that the extortion group known as BlackFile has rebranded as Redact. This transition follows an internal dispute among affiliates, with the group continuing to leverage vishing tactics and coercive extortion schemes against their targets.
stories.why: Tracking threat actor rebrands is essential for maintaining accurate detection signatures and understanding evolving adversary tactics in extortion-based attacks.

stories.title: Malware Can Abuse Windows Hello for Business Keys for Persistent Entra ID Access
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered that malware with local user access can leverage Windows Hello for Business cryptographic keys to authenticate against Entra ID. This allows attackers to register rogue devices, acquire Primary Refresh Tokens, and maintain persistent, unauthorized access to cloud environments.
stories.why: This technique bypasses traditional MFA by abusing legitimate, hardware-backed authentication flows, enabling attackers to escalate privileges and maintain long-term cloud persistence.

stories.title: A Security Pro Hacked North Korean Hackers. He Found They’d Breached Hundreds of Networks Worldwide
stories.abstract: A security researcher successfully infiltrated North Korean state-sponsored infrastructure, maintaining persistent access for two years. His analysis reveals a massive, global campaign of unauthorized network intrusions conducted by the threat actors across hundreds of distinct organizations.
stories.why: This confirms the scale and persistence of North Korean cyber-espionage operations, highlighting the critical need for robust egress filtering and anomaly detection.

stories.title: ClickFix attack pushes macOS infostealer for crypto theft attacks
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging ClickFix social engineering tactics to distribute Go-based malware on macOS. The malicious payload harvests cryptocurrency wallets, browser credentials, and sensitive data stored within the Apple Keychain, posing a significant risk to user privacy and financial assets.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates evolving cross-platform social engineering techniques that bypass standard user caution to exfiltrate high-value credentials and assets.

stories.title: Flock Pitched a Plan To Turn Uber and Lyft Drivers Into Roaming Surveillance Vehicles
stories.abstract: Flock Safety explored a strategy to transform hundreds of thousands of rideshare and delivery vehicles into mobile surveillance nodes. The initiative aimed to leverage these drivers to capture and aggregate license plate data, significantly expanding the reach of the company's existing automated monitoring network.
stories.why: This highlights the rapid expansion of private surveillance networks and the potential for third-party platforms to act as mass data collection vectors.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 AitM Phishing Hijacks Accounts to Collect Payroll and Finance Emails
stories.abstract: Attackers are utilizing adversary-in-the-middle phishing tactics to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. By routing traffic through residential proxies, the campaign bypasses standard detection to target financial personnel and intercept sensitive payroll and accounting communications.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates sophisticated evasion techniques that bypass traditional MFA, specifically targeting high-value financial data within corporate email environments.
stories.action: Implement FIDO2-compliant hardware security keys to mitigate adversary-in-the-middle phishing risks.

stories.title: New OVSwrap Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Open vSwitch
stories.abstract: A memory corruption vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Open vSwitch datapath allows local attackers to escalate privileges to root. The flaw, dubbed OVSwrap, is accompanied by a public exploit targeting hundreds of common kernel configurations.
stories.why: Local privilege escalation via a widely used kernel component poses a significant risk to multi-user systems and containerized environments.
stories.action: Patch the Linux kernel to the latest version provided by your distribution.

stories.title: The Frontier AI Vulnerability Burst: Industrializing Autonomous Zero-Day Discovery in Open-Source Software
stories.abstract: Unit 42 researchers developed an AI-driven system called NOVA to automate the identification of security flaws. The tool successfully scanned open-source repositories, uncovering over 14,000 previously unknown vulnerabilities within the software supply chain.
stories.why: Automated, large-scale vulnerability discovery by AI signals a shift toward faster exploitation cycles and increased pressure on open-source maintainers.

stories.title: 22 Seconds to Compromise: How Automated SSH Actors Move From Login to Persistence Before You Can Blink [Guest Diary], (Thu, Aug 6th)
stories.abstract: A SANS ISC guest report highlights the extreme speed at which automated attackers can compromise SSH services. Threat actors are now capable of moving from initial unauthorized login to establishing persistent access in under half a minute, leaving virtually no time for manual intervention.
stories.why: Rapid automated exploitation cycles render traditional manual incident response ineffective, necessitating automated defensive measures and robust authentication hardening.

stories.title: Critical Gitea Flaw Let Unauthenticated Attackers Read Server Files via Org-Mode Markup
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in Gitea versions 1.22.1 through 1.27.0 allows unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary file reads on the host server. By submitting malicious Org-mode markup to a public repository, remote actors can access sensitive files accessible to the Gitea service account.
stories.why: This flaw enables unauthorized access to configuration files, credentials, and system data without requiring authentication or repository write permissions.
stories.action: Update Gitea to version 1.27.1 immediately.

stories.title: Zbtlink security advisory (AV26-779)
stories.abstract: Zbtlink has identified a security vulnerability impacting a wide range of its router and gateway firmware versions. The affected models include various CPE and WG series devices, necessitating a review of current deployments against the manufacturer's latest security guidance.
stories.why: Unpatched network infrastructure devices are frequent targets for remote exploitation and botnet recruitment.
stories.action: Check Zbtlink support resources and apply available firmware updates for your specific device model.
